items.note: The section 'Why a tiny deficit is enough' runs the paper's chain (lines 1319-1346): the deficits exceed 20*2^{-50}, log m<20, m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta), and so s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. It also adds the missing link 's/W=m(1-eta)'.

The page gives the definition eta=(Wm-s)/(Wm), but the two exact values and the claim 'both greater than 20*2^{-50}' are only asserted. No s, W or m values or arithmetic are shown (about 1.5e-11 and 3.7e-12 against about 1.8e-14). The paper also only asserts them.
The page gives both premises, 'm<2^{20} and log 2<1', so log m<20 log 2<20 follows, exactly as in the paper. Like the paper, the page does not say why m<2^{20} holds (m=h^3=10^6, paper line 656).
This is the paper's displayed chain. The page adds the justification the paper leaves implicit: 'using e^{-x}>1-x for x>0' with x=2^{-50}log m<20*2^{-50}, then eta>20*2^{-50} for the last inequality.
'Since s/W=m(1-eta)' correctly rewrites the definition of eta. Combined with S4.4.3 it gives both inequalities and 0<tau=sigma<1, as in the paper.

errors.quote: Replace each scalar by an array of logical volume $V$, the total size of the array, and use [Elementary stream operations](elementary-stream-ops.md) to split it into $W$ role streams of volume $V/W$.
errors.problem: This conflates two arrays. In the paper (lines 123-128) the node array of volume V (after padding) has its rows distributed cyclically among the W roles, so each scalar wire carries a role stream of volume V/W, not an array of volume V.

The paper (lines 1345-1346) says sigma is 'a rational upper bound for the logarithmic exponent of the complex recurrence', not the exponent itself; the exponent log_m(s_c/W_c) is strictly smaller than sigma.
